audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor combines parent-attributable earnings with 100% of consolidated depreciation, amortization, working-capital movements and capital spending, affecting OE in every historical year and therefore the projected operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Nucor owns a 51 % controlling interest in each of Nucor-Yamato, CSI and NJSM.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter inconsistency, not merely a possibility. Nucor reported $294 million of 2025 earnings attributable to noncontrolling interests, equal to 15.5% of the $1,901.6 million OE anchor, showing that the minority claim is substantial. The exact OE error is unquantified because minority portions of depreciation, working capital and capital expenditures are not supplied. Its direction is mixed because consolidated add-backs can overstate parent OE while consolidated capital and working-capital deductions can understate it. A correction of this scale is reasonably capable of changing scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2017-2025 OE on one consistent perimeter—preferably consolidated earnings and cash-flow adjustments followed by an explicit noncontrolling-interest deduction—and rerun every scenario and buy-below value.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may include cash belonging to minority owners
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $413.1 million attributable to minority ownership, computed as 49% of $843 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash and short-term investments to NUE common equity without removing the noncontrolling claim on cash held by majority-owned joint ventures.
audit_findings.evidence: Approximately $931 million and $970 million of the cash and cash equivalents position as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, was held by our majority-owned joint ventures.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing identifies $843 million of cash held by majority-owned joint ventures. Applying the disclosed 49% minority ownership gives a maximum identified minority portion of $413.1 million, or about $1.81 per diluted share and 1.4% of the $30.0 billion base equity value. Even excluding all $843 million of joint-venture cash would reduce base value by only about $3.69 per share and would not close the $130.56 gap between the $131.38 base value and the $261.94 market price. Operational restrictions remain unresolved but do not make the identified amount material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain joint-venture-level cash, investment, distribution and obligation schedules as of July 4, 2026; remove the minority-owned and operationally unavailable portions and document the adjusted bridge.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest can bypass the stated interest-expense rail
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized borrowing costs avoid current interest expense; if the associated project capital is excluded from the OE reinvestment charge, the cost is omitted from both OE and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense decreased in 2025 compared to 2024 due to an increase in capitalized interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that capitalized interest reduced reported interest expense in both 2025 and the first six months of 2026, but they do not provide the capitalized amount or the valuation ledger needed to establish whether it was deducted through capital expenditures. The possible omission would overstate equity-level OE, but the record cannot establish its magnitude or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile interest paid, expensed interest and capitalized interest by project for 2025 and 2026; map capitalized interest into the maintenance-versus-growth capital ledger and rerun the valuation if any amount was excluded from both OE and the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Investment fair-value movements may be counted alongside the stakes bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Investment marks retained in OE can duplicate returns on assets separately included in the $590 million stakes bridge, while restructuring charges retained in the anchor can depress sustainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Impacting the increase in marketing, administrative and other expenses in 2025 as compared to 2024 were fair market value adjustments of our Level 1 investments and expenses associated with restructuring initiatives in the steel mills segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 filing confirms that Level 1 investment fair-value adjustments and restructuring expenses affected marketing, administrative and other expenses, but does not disclose their separate amounts. The 2026 filing demonstrates the same mechanism through a disclosed $61 million noncash Helion gain, although that gain is outside the 2025 anchor. Without the 2025 adjustment ledger and the composition of the $590 million stakes bridge, neither duplication nor materiality can be established. Direction is mixed because investment marks can be gains or losses, while removing qualifying restructuring charges would increase value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025 investment-mark and restructuring ledger, reconcile every marked investment to the $590 million stakes bridge, remove duplicated investment returns from OE, classify restructuring costs facility by facility, and rerun if adjustments are material.

audit_findings.title: Recorded tax claims may not be reflected in prospective owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $222 million, comprising $173 million of unrecognized tax benefits and $49 million of related interest and penalties
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlement could consume cash after the associated accounting expense was accrued, causing a gross-cash bridge or prospective OE forecast to omit the remaining common-equity claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Note: In addition to the amounts shown in the table above, $173 million of unrecognized tax benefits have been recorded as liabilities, and we are uncertain as to if or when such amounts may be settled.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed year-end exposure totals $222 million. If the entire amount were deducted from the bridge, base value would decline by about $0.97 per share, or 0.74% of the $30.0 billion base equity value. That cannot change the conclusion against a $261.94 market price, although the bridge-date liability and settlement timing remain to be confirmed.
audit_findings.action: Update the uncertain-tax-position, interest and penalty balances to July 4, 2026; verify whether expected payments enter forecast working-capital cash flows and otherwise deduct the expected settlement from surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor retains disclosed asset losses and impairments
audit_findings.magnitude: $67 million pre-tax in 2025, including $47 million identified as noncash in the cash-flow reconciliation
audit_findings.mechanism: Unnormalized closure, repurposing and impairment charges reduce the latest-year OE anchor and therefore proportionally reduce projected OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in 2025 net earnings were $67 million of losses and impairments of assets ($137 million in 2024).
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed $67 million charge equals 3.5% of the $1,901.6 million anchor. Even treating the full pre-tax amount as a dollar-for-dollar anchor increase—an upper-bound treatment that ignores tax and economic deterioration—would proportionally increase the $26.718 billion base operating PV by about $942 million, or approximately $4.12 per share. The resulting value would remain far below the $261.94 market price. Recurrence in 2024 and 2025 also argues against automatically normalizing the entire charge.
audit_findings.action: Review the $39 million steel-products and $23 million steel-mills facility charges and the remaining amount individually; adjust only noncash, nonrecurring charges unrelated to continuing deterioration or recurring rationalization, then document the immaterial scenario effect.
